Submitted answer: No. Verified answer: No.

The premises are two universal conditionals (leadership seminars → managerial skills, team-building → teamwork) and an existential claim that some instances have neither outcome. Nothing says John is one of those instances.

A countermodel shows this. Let John attend both activities and gain both benefits, and let a second employee do neither and gain neither. Both conditionals hold, the "neither" instance exists (the second employee), and for John "not L or not T" is false. So the conclusion is not entailed.

The re-derivation that answers "Yes" has to assume John is the "neither" case, and the premises do not state that.
